The person wrote "You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back" just once. That single handwritten sentence was then reproduced seven times, and the person is now reading the duplicated result. The seven identical written copies are not seven separate utterances or seven people speaking: they stem from one original handwritten statement that was copied. The "Sigh, I know I'm in trouble" reflects the person's realization, upon seeing their own sentence reproduced sevenfold, that they are implicated by their own words.
